title: Compiler Architecture
concept: The XIOM compiler architecture — frontend (lexer, parser, checker) and backend (codegen, LLVM, optimization) pipeline overview.
why: Understanding the compiler's architecture helps you debug build issues, interpret error messages, and know which phase is responsible for what.
theory:
## The XIOM Compiler

### Architecture Overview

```
Source Code (.xi)
    │
    ▼
┌─────────────┐
│   LEXER     │  Tokenize source into tokens
└──────┬──────┘
       ▼
┌─────────────┐
│   PARSER    │  Build AST from tokens
└──────┬──────┘
       ▼
┌─────────────┐
│ NAMERESOLVE │  Resolve names, imports
└──────┬──────┘
       ▼
┌─────────────┐
│ TYPE CHECK  │  Type checking, type inference
└──────┬──────┘
       ▼
┌─────────────┐
│BORROW CHECK │  Ownership, borrows, lifetimes
└──────┬──────┘
       ▼
┌─────────────┐
│ CONTRACT    │  Verify contracts, invariants
└──────┬──────┘
       ▼
┌─────────────┐
│   CODEGEN   │  Generate LLVM IR
└──────┬──────┘
       ▼
┌─────────────┐
│    LLVM     │  Optimize, codegen to machine code
└──────┬──────┘
       ▼
   Binary
```

### Phase Responsibilities

| Phase | Input | Output | Errors Caught |
|-------|-------|--------|---------------|
| Lexer | Source text | Token stream | Invalid characters |
| Parser | Token stream | AST | Syntax errors |
| NameResolve | AST | Resolved AST | Undefined names |
| Type Check | Resolved AST | Typed AST | Type mismatch |
| Borrow Check | Typed AST | Borrow-validated AST | Use-after-move |
| Contract | Borrow AST | Verified AST | Contract violation |
| Codegen | Verified AST | LLVM IR | N/A (rare) |
| LLVM | LLVM IR | Machine code | N/A |

### Compilation Modes

```sh
# Full compilation (all phases)
xiom build

# Check only (stop after type checking)
xiom check

# Parse only (rapid syntax checking)
xiom check --parse-only
```

### Compiler as Library

```xiom
// Use the XIOM compiler API programmatically
use xiom_compiler;

fn main() {
  let source = "fn add(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int { return a + b; }";
  let compiler = xiom_compiler::Session::new();
  let result = compiler.compile_str(source);

  match result {
    Ok(binary) => io.println("Compiled successfully"),
    Err(errors) => {
      for error in errors {
        io.println(error.to_str());
      }
    },
  }
}
```
tips: Use `xiom check` instead of `xiom build` in your editor for faster error feedback
The lexer and parser are the fastest phases — syntax errors are caught in <1ms
Understanding which phase catches your error helps you write better bug reports
The compiler is a library — you can embed XIOM compilation in your own tools
common_mistakes: Confusing parse errors (lexer/parser) with type errors (type checker)
Not using xiom check for editor integration — it's much faster than full builds
Assuming all errors come from the same phase — knowing the phase helps debugging
